title: Invocation Status and Instance Status are two separate state vocabularies covering before and after an Instance exists
content:
The four prospective Instances each carry a document type the live Instances do not have: an Invocation Status (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.1.4.1.1 and siblings), whose value is `Planning`. Active and Completed Instances have no such document — their state is expressed by which directory holds them, using the Instance Status vocabulary of `Active`, `Completed` and `Suspended`.

So the Atlas maintains two disjoint status languages. Invocation Status describes the progress of the *process of creating* an Instance; Instance Status describes the condition of an Instance that already exists. Nothing sits in both at once.

The distinction avoids a real modelling error. If prospective Instances were given an Instance Status, the natural value would be something like `Inactive` — which the Atlas already uses for a different meaning elsewhere: the Light Agent and Token SkyLink Primitives are `Inactive` as *whole primitives that have been switched off*, not as things being built. Keeping the vocabularies separate stops "not yet" from being confused with "turned off."

It also means the two questions an observer might ask have separate answers in separate places: what is Skybase running (read the Active directories) versus what is Skybase in the middle of starting (read the In Progress directories and their Invocation Statuses). The `Planning` value additionally implies later Invocation Status values exist for subsequent stages, giving the Invocation itself a progress track distinct from the Instance's lifecycle.
description: `Planning` is an Invocation Status held only by in-progress subtrees; Active, Completed and Suspended are Instance Statuses, so a prospective Instance is never described as inactive.
